SOAP Clinical Note

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Dry, itchy, red skin on arms and hands for “a few days,” noticed after swimming; no spread to chest, legs, or face; no fever, spots, sweating, vomiting, skin discharge, or bleeding; using coconut butter without relief.
- Past medical history: Denies previous skin conditions (eczema, dermatitis) or other chronic illnesses.
- Medications:
  • Microgynon (combined oral contraceptive pill) – dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Social history: Lives alone; primary-school teacher; denies tobacco, alcohol, and recreational drug use; reports increased work-related stress and long hours.
- Allergies: Self-reported lactose intolerance; no drug allergies reported.
- Family history: Father – asthma; Mother – hay fever; no known family skin disorders.

Objective:
- Physical examination: Not performed (remote consultation).
- Investigations: None performed or ordered.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Dry, itchy rash on arms/hands
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Suspected contact/irritant dermatitis (possibly chlorine-related from swimming).
   - Differential diagnosis: Atopic dermatitis, allergic contact dermatitis, nonspecific xerosis.
   - Investigations planned: None at this stage.
   - Treatment planned:
     • Topical steroid cream (specific agent/potency not documented) to affected areas.
     • Regular emollient application throughout the day.
     • Oral over-the-counter antihistamines (e.g., chlorpheniramine [Piriton], loratadine) for pruritus.
     • Provide patient information leaflet on dermatitis and skin care.
   - Follow-up: Return visit in one week if no improvement or sooner if symptoms worsen.

2. Work-related stress
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Occupational stress.
   - Treatment planned: Acknowledged; offered supportive advice; no formal intervention requested by patient at this time.

Quality checks:
● Missing but clinically expected: Vital signs, detailed skin examination findings, exact steroid/emollient names and dosing instructions, complete allergy list including medications and environmental allergens.  
● Internal conflicts: None noted.  
● Transcript quality: Generally clear; occasional brief inaudible or interrupted segments that did not affect clinical content.
